analysis: This batch is documentation-only: a changelog entry, the new docs/architecture/addon-hold.md, README index link, a model-autopilot.md busy-reason note, and docs/developer/test.md test instructions. No provider source is in the supplied evidence, so the implementation of the add-on hold is unverified. The docs describe a new local attack surface: an owner-only AF_UNIX socket (~/.darkbloom/runtime/addon.sock) where a signed add-on can hold the provider. Documented controls: peer verification (AddonPeerPolicy: code requirement, hardened runtime, same user, add-on identifier must equal the verified signer), owner-only runtime directory and persisted hold records, 30-600 s leases, the machine-lock-gated lease expiry, and an operator `darkbloom addon release --force` override. The hold keeps the coordinator connection and App Attest worker. It reports status draining with busy fields rather than sending provider_drain, and it unloads models, retaining loaded-models.json. The documented design does not appear to weaken A-003/A-016 or TB-011: the hold only reduces serving, doesn't grant authorization, and doesn't widen plaintext exposure. Residual availability considerations: a same-user signed add-on (or one that keeps holding ownership.lock) can keep the provider out of routing, which is consistent with the documented trust of the add-on and the operator-override. Items for later passes: verify in the Swift code (not supplied) that AddonPeerPolicy validates audit token/code requirement without TOCTOU, that socket and record file permissions and symlink handling are enforced, that line-size/connection limits exist, that the hold-restore path closes admission before any model load, and that busy_addon fields are not attacker-controlled strings leaking to the coordinator unsanitized. Also note the T-057-like availability angle: indefinite holds when a lock is held. Test docs state the peer check is only tested negatively, so positive-path verification is an open gap, and the threat model may eventually need a TB entry for the add-on IPC boundary. No concrete regressions are identified in the supplied documentation.
